prompt: Why do you want to join this IT scholarship programme, and what do you hope to gain from it?
hint: Say what you want, why you want it, and what you will do with it. One clear reason explained well beats four reasons listed.

prompt: What are your goals for the next five years? Explain how you plan to reach them.
hint: A goal with a plan under it reads as serious. A goal on its own reads as a wish.

prompt: Why did you choose to study software and information technology instead of another field?
hint: A real moment when you chose is stronger than a general statement that IT is important.

prompt: Describe a project you have built. What was it for, what was the hardest part, and what would you do differently?
hint: The hardest part and what you would change are the interesting bits. Do not spend half the essay describing the features.

prompt: Describe a difficult problem you solved. How did you work it out?
hint: Walk through the steps you actually took, including the things you tried that failed.

prompt: Describe something you taught yourself without a teacher. How did you do it, and what made it hard?
hint: Self teaching is what this programme will ask of you, so show your method, not just the result.

prompt: Write about a mistake you made and what you learned from it.
hint: Be honest about the mistake. An essay that hides the mistake has nothing left to say about learning.

prompt: Describe a time you worked in a team. What was your part, and what did you find difficult?
hint: Name your own contribution clearly. Avoid writing only about what the group did.

prompt: Write about a person who has influenced you. What did you learn from them?
hint: One specific thing they said or did carries more weight than a list of their good qualities.

prompt: What makes a good teacher? Give your reasons.
hint: Pick two or three qualities and explain each one. Do not list ten.

prompt: How important is English for a software developer in Cambodia? Explain your view.
hint: You are writing this in English, so the essay is its own evidence. Keep the sentences short and correct.

prompt: How has technology changed daily life in Cambodia in the last ten years? Give examples.
hint: Two or three real examples you have seen yourself beat a general claim about progress.

prompt: Some people say AI will take away programming jobs. Do you agree? Give your reasons.
hint: Answer the question directly in the first sentence, then defend it. Mention the other side once and say why you still disagree.

prompt: Should every student learn to write computer programs? Give your reasons.
hint: A clear no, well argued, scores as well as a clear yes. Do not sit in the middle.

prompt: Is learning online as good as learning in a classroom? Explain your view.
hint: You have done both. Use what actually happened to you as the evidence.

prompt: Does social media do more good or more harm to young people? Give your reasons.
hint: Choose one side. An essay that says both sides are equal usually says nothing.

prompt: Is it better for a young Cambodian developer to work abroad or to stay and work in Cambodia?
hint: This programme leads to work with Korean companies, so your answer will be read with interest. Be honest.

prompt: Should you choose a job for the money or for the work itself? Give your reasons.
hint: A real example from someone you know makes this much stronger than general argument.

prompt: Do people learn more from failure than from success? Explain your view.
hint: Do not just assert that failure teaches. Show one thing a failure taught you that a success could not.

prompt: Do you work better alone or in a team? Explain with examples.
hint: Either answer is fine. Saying you are good at both, without examples, is the weak answer.

prompt: What makes a piece of software good? Give your reasons.
hint: Think beyond "no bugs". Speed, clarity and whether ordinary people can use it all count.

prompt: Explain what a computer program is to someone who has never used a computer.
hint: Explaining simply is a real skill and it is being tested. Avoid every technical word you can.

prompt: Describe an app you use often. What makes it good, and what would you change about it?
hint: The change you would make shows how you think. Spend half the essay on it.

prompt: How much should people worry about their privacy online? Give your reasons.
hint: Take a position early. Vague worry is hard to argue.

prompt: What is the biggest challenge facing the IT industry in Cambodia, and how could it be solved?
hint: Name one challenge, not four. The solution half is where most of the marks will be.

prompt: Describe how you study. What works for you, and what does not?
hint: Be concrete about your routine. This is a question about self knowledge, not about study tips.

prompt: How do you deal with pressure and deadlines? Give an example.
hint: One story told properly is worth more than a list of techniques.

prompt: What do you enjoy doing outside your studies, and what does it give you?
hint: The second half of the question matters. Say what it gives you, not just what it is.

prompt: What advice would you give to yourself three years ago?
hint: This works best if you say what actually went wrong, then the advice that would have helped.

prompt: If you are accepted, what will you bring to this programme and to the other students?
hint: Answer about what you give, not what you get. That is the trap in this question.
